volunteer_note: Per-person effect sizes (Cohen d, sleep-deprived vs baseline) from the PUBLIC dataset Zenodo 4326598 (Bourdillon et al., CC BY 4.0; 5 people; hr and rmssd only; orthostatic-test RR intervals). NOT team volunteers. Voice, typing, blink, puffy-face remain unvalidated. RESULT: On the public sleep-deprivation dataset (5 usable people) the model score moved in the OPPOSITE direction to expected (lower, not higher, when deprived in 5 of 5 people), so NO detection of sleep-deprivation fatigue is claimed. Raw HR was higher in 3 of 5 people and RMSSD lower in 2 of 5. Confounds: morning orthostatic recordings mix supine/standing posture, only 3 deprivation days, baseline = first half of own rested minutes.
